name: GLib
listed_description: Library of utility functions and structures, designed to be portable, efficient and powerful
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. Read GLib's NEWS (about 770 KB): the only performance statements are relative to older GLib (for example the 2.19 GHashTable open-addressing rewrite 'slightly faster' and 'benchmarks suggest it also uses less memory', no figures) and 'speed up' notes for GObject, GMarkup, GKeyFile and utf8 without baselines or numbers; GSlice was dropped in favour of system malloc. Third-party shootouts do not help: hpjansson/hash-table-rehash README has no results (they are generated locally and the blog posts are blocked), and the JacksonAllan c_cpp_hash_tables_benchmark discussion excludes GHashTable and says node-based tables like it cannot keep up with open-addressing tables. wiki.gnome.org, gitlab.gnome.org and hpjansson.org are blocked in this environment, so the GHashTable MR benchmark numbers could not be opened.

name: huffandpuff
listed_description: Minimal Huffman encoder and decoder. Public domain.
reason: No numbers and no baseline. The repo has five files (huffman.c, huffman.h, Makefile, README.md, .gitignore), the README is five lines claiming only that it is extremely minimal, uses no stdlib calls and suits embedded use, public domain; no benchmarks, no comparison with zlib or any other Huffman coder. 104 stars, last commit 2013-06-14. A web search for the name found nothing else (no blog, shootout or paper mentioning it).
